_comment: Repo-side freshness pins for signoff/gf180-sar-adc.manifest.json (issue
#331). `python3 signoff/run_signoff.py --check` re-derives every value
below with nothing but CPython, which is what lets CI -- which installs
neither `klt` nor the PDK -- fail a manifest that cites an artifact that
has since changed, instead of letting the committed verdict rot.
Hand-written here: the STRUCTURE and every `note`. Machine-written by
`--regen`: every hash, every `envelope_asserts` value, `expected_rows`,
and the `report` block. Do not hand-edit a value to make `--check` pass;
re-run `--regen` and record what moved.
citations.<item key>
file            the cited envelope, repo-root-relative (must equal the
manifest's own citation).
manifest_pins   the `content_hash` the MANIFEST pins on this citation,
i.e. what `klt signoff` itself checks. `null` is
allowed only with a `manifest_pin_note` saying why.
report_citation_note
required ONLY for a citation whose report row renders
no `citation` object (item 7's errored run, or item
11's compound row while it grades `unmet` --
`_grade_power_delivery` only ever builds a `citation`
on the `met` path). `--check` asserts every other
citation's file and pin against the grader's own
record of what it read, so a re-pointed citation
cannot pass without `--regen`; a row the comparison
cannot reach must say so here rather than be skipped
in silence.
envelope_asserts  fields inside the cited envelope that must still read
exactly as they did when the report was minted --
including each envelope's own statement about the input
IT consumed.
artifacts       repo files whose bytes the citation's claim depends on,
with their sha256. THIS is the rot detector: edit the
GDS without re-running DRC and the next pull request
goes red. An EMPTY `artifacts` is allowed only with an
`artifacts_note` saying why -- otherwise a citation
with no pinned bytes would get zero hash coverage
while `--check` still printed `[ok]` for it.
parts           ONLY for a COMPOUND item (T1 item 11, klayout-tools
#2025): a list of the shape above (`file`/
`manifest_pins`/`manifest_pin_note`/`envelope_asserts`/
`artifacts`, each tagged with a human-readable `role`),
one per part of the manifest's own list-valued
citation, in the SAME ORDER -- `run_signoff.py`
compares them positionally. A citation carrying
`parts` carries no top-level `file`/`artifacts` of its
own; every other key above still applies per-part
instead of once.
expected_rows     every row the committed report renders, with its
status/reason. A row flipping to `met` is as much a
drift signal as one flipping to `unmet`, so both
directions are pinned.
report            which committed report the pins above describe, with
the sha256 of BOTH committed renderings: `sha256` for
signoff.json (the artifact of record) and
`text_sha256` for signoff.txt (what a reviewer reads
as a diff). Both are `--regen` output; neither is
hand-edited.

note: T1 item 3 (DRC clean), ANALOG partition. Item 3 is kind-independent
in the checklist, so a bare `3` key would render this one citation in
both partitions' rows -- see the manifest's own _comment on why each
side is keyed separately instead.
The pinned `content_hash` is the sha256 of layout/adc-top/adc_block.gds
as committed -- the report's own `provenance.input.content_hash` and a
fresh hash of the committed GDS are the same bytes, which is the
freshness claim.
COVERAGE IS REPORTED, NOT GRADED (klayout-tools#2002). `klt signoff`
renders item 3 `met` on `status: clean` alone. The deck's own gaps --
6 drawn layers with no rule, 4 rules the deck carries but did not
evaluate, and a 10-chapter deck scope -- are quoted verbatim in the
evidence record under signoff/records/, which is where this repo
discharges the claimant-enforced disclosure the item requires.
T1 item 3 (DRC clean), DIGITAL partition: the routed SAR-sequencer
macro's own `klt drc` run, minted by design/sar-logic/flow/
pnr_sar_ctrl.py alongside the `klt place-and-route` response (#274).
`status: clean`, violation_count 0, deck gf180mcu.
WHY THE REPO-SIDE HASH CHECK EARNS ITS KEEP HERE. This envelope's
`file` field is an absolute path from the worktree the P&R run was
executed in, which does not exist anywhere in this repo -- so `klt
signoff` cannot re-hash the artifact and reports `input: not
re-hashed (content_hash compared against this envelope's own claim
only)`. The committed layout/adc-top/sar_ctrl/sar_ctrl.gds DOES hash
to exactly the envelope's `provenance.input.content_hash`, which is
what `run_signoff.py --check` re-derives on every pull request. The
grader's freshness gate is weaker than this repo's here, not stronger.
COVERAGE (claimant-enforced, quoted in the evidence record): 10 drawn
layers with no rule in the deck, 7 rules skipped, same 10-chapter
deck scope as the analog run. The standard-cell stream draws more
rule-free layers than the analog block does, which is disclosed
rather than folded into 'clean'.
T1 item 4 (LVS clean), ANALOG partition: the drawn analog block's
extraction compared against its flat SPICE reference. `status: match`,
klayout engine, mismatch_count 0.
gf180-sar-adc#338 CLOSED THE EXCEPTION this row used to carry. The
prior citation (layout/lvs/reports/20260817-185722-40cfeb8/
adc_block.lvs.json) was written by `klt 0.2.0` (layout/toolchain.json's
then-pin, 85b8125), which did not populate `provenance.input` at all
-- the one citation in this manifest with no `content_hash`, pinned
instead by the repo-side `environment.layout_sha256`/
`environment.reference_sha256` check below. layout/toolchain.json is
now bumped to `b15edf5e` (klayout-tools#1969, PR #2005, `provenance.
input.content_hash`; and klayout-tools#2027, PR #2058, the
`input.role` field that makes the hash's KIND explicit -- absorbed in
the same bump per #338's own scope), so this citation now carries a
real `content_hash` (`provenance.input.content_hash`, role
`"netlist"` -- this is the pre-extracted `layout.netlist` request
shape, so the hashed input is the SPICE netlist `klt lvs` compared,
not a layout stream; klayout-tools#2027's own fix is what makes that
distinction machine-readable via `role` instead of assumed).
`klt signoff --manifest` grades this row on that hash directly now,
the same mechanism every other populated citation in this manifest
uses -- no repo-side workaround needed for this row any longer. The
`environment.layout_sha256`/`environment.reference_sha256` assertions
below are kept anyway: belt-and-suspenders, not a substitute.
4.digital IS DELIBERATELY UNCITED. No netlist-vs-layout compare of
the routed sar_ctrl macro exists in this repo; citing the analog
block's compare in the digital row would claim coverage that run
does not have.
Single-engine. design-evidence-tiers.md notes a second, independent
engine's concurring verdict (klayout-tools#343) would strengthen this
from 'one toolchain agrees with itself' to a cross-checked result;
this repo has one engine and says so rather than implying otherwise.
power_connectivity/body_verification: gf180-sar-adc#338's related
note (this 0.2.0-era report lacked the klayout-tools#1952/#1965/
#1983 blocks) is now moot for the wrong reason to celebrate -- the
new report DOES carry both blocks, but both render

report_citation_note: THE COMPOUND ITEM (issue #2025, gf180-sar-adc#347). `klt signoff`
renders NO `citation` object at all for an `unmet` item-11 row --
item 11's own grader (`_grade_power_delivery`) only ever builds a
`citation` on the `met` path. This note was written while the row
graded `unmet`/`supply_spec_incomplete`, when `--check`'s
row-vs-manifest comparison could not reach it at all.
SINCE ISSUE #356 THE ROW GRADES `met`, so the grader DOES render a
citation and that comparison reaches this row like any other -- the
declared-absence rule this note existed to satisfy no longer
applies. The note is kept rather than deleted because the mechanical
gap it describes is real and will bite again the moment this row
regresses: if the supply spec ever loses its `ties[]`, the row drops
back to `unmet`, the citation object disappears, and only the
`parts[]`/`expected_rows` pins below still cover it. Item 7's
`report_citation_note` documents the same gap, still live there.
What covers this citation either way: `parts[]` below pins each
cited artifact's `envelope_asserts`/`artifacts` exactly as every
other citation does, and `expected_rows` pins `T1#11.analog`'s
status/reason in both directions -- so either part rotting, or the
row silently flipping back to `unmet`, fails CI.
note: T1 item 11 (Power delivery, structural), ANALOG partition. Compound
citation (klayout-tools#2025): `klt signoff` requires the `klt erc`
supply run (`parts[0]`) PLUS the LVS report item 4 already cites
(`parts[1]`) before it will grade this row at all.
GRADES `met` SINCE ISSUE #356, and the history matters because this
row's reason changed three times without anyone relaxing a check.
It read `unmet`/`supply_spec_incomplete` while the committed supply
spec declared no `ties[]` -- `ADC_BLOCK` drew no implant layers, so
the real gf180mcu tap boolean `COMP n Nplus` had nothing to
intersect, and DR-0032 recorded the omission as the honest form.
#340 then answered the same question from geometry instead and found
the 25 n-wells untapped and both substrate-tie rings strapped to
nothing: failed-on-evidence, not uncomputed.
#356 fixed the layout (DR-0035, superseding DR-0032). Every well now
carries an `Nplus`-marked, contacted n+ tap routed to `vdd`, both
rings are closed, `Pplus`-marked and strapped into the `vss` island,
and the supply spec declares `ties[]` with `tap_requires: ["32/0"]`.
The committed `klt erc` run reports `erc_status: "clean"` with ZERO
`erc.missing_tie` from a rule that was CHECKED (the run's
`erc_coverage.checked` carries `erc.missing_tie:["nwell_tap"]`,
asserted by `layout/erc/cases.json`) -- so the declaration is
complete AND its verdict is clean, which is what `met` requires.
WHAT `met` HERE DOES NOT CLAIM. The substrate tie is not graded by
`erc.missing_tie` at all: `klt erc` needs a drawn `well_layer` and
the p-substrate is not drawn, so the two guard rings are covered
only by their membership of the one `vss` island (zero
`erc.unconnected_net`) and by the direct geometric measurement in
`layout/erc/well-tap-audit.json`. `pdn` is `no` and
`power_connectivity` is `unchecked` for want of a `klt
place-and-route` response, which this analog partition does not
have and item 11 does not require of it.
11.digital IS DELIBERATELY UNCITED. No LVS of the routed `sar_ctrl`
macro exists in this repo, and for the digital column
`power_connectivity.status: "unchecked"` does NOT satisfy item 11
(unlike item 4, where `unchecked` means 'the question does not
apply here') -- citing the analog block's LVS in the digital row
would claim coverage that partition does not have.
The `klt erc` supply run against `ADC_BLOCK`, re-minted at issue
#378 against the Metal2-strapped geometry (record
append-only). `erc_status: "clean"`, `erc_finding_count: 0`, no
coverage skip recorded -- and, since issue #356, the spec declares
`ties[]`, so the zero `erc.missing_tie` in that count is a COMPUTED
verdict over 25 wells rather than a question never asked. That is
precisely the difference between `supply_spec_incomplete` and `met`
for this row. #378 moved the block-level straps off Poly2 and onto
Metal2, which is an ELECTRICAL change (see
layout/power/records/20260923-084734-5f13cf9.md and DR-0037); this
structural row reports exactly what it reported before it, which is
why the run was re-taken rather than reasoned about.

report_citation_note: THE ONE CITATION `--check` CANNOT COMPARE AGAINST THE COMMITTED
REPORT, and the reason is mechanical. Every other cited row carries
the grader's own `citation.file`/`citation.content_hash`, which
`--check` asserts against this manifest so a re-pointed citation
cannot pass without `--regen`. This row renders
`unmet`/`check_failed` with `citation: null` -- the `klt pex` run
errored, so the grader records no citation object at all and the
report does not remember which file it read.
What still covers this citation: `envelope_asserts` below pins the
errored run's own `status`/`errored`/`corner_count` and its
`provenance.input.content_hash`, `artifacts` pins the comparator
GDS byte for byte, and `expected_rows` pins the row in both
directions -- so a flip to `met` fails CI. What is NOT covered is a
swap of this citation for a different errored pex run whose
envelope happens to assert the same fields, which would need a
re-pointed `file` here and is a reviewed edit by construction.
This note exists because the gap has to be DECLARED: `--check`
fails any manifest citation that the report renders no citation
for unless its freshness entry says why.
note: T1 item 7 (post-layout verification), analog partition. CITED
DELIBERATELY EVEN THOUGH IT DOES NOT PASS: the row renders
`unmet`/`check_failed`, which states the true position -- a `klt pex`
run was attempted and errored -- where leaving the item uncited would
have said only `no_evidence`.
Two independent reasons this citation cannot go green, both recorded
so nobody re-derives them:
* The run ERRORED. `klt pex`'s DUT swap requires the schematic and
extracted top-level `.subckt` interfaces to be pin-identical,
which `klt extract`'s promoted body/tap/internal nets never are
here. Filed upstream as klayout-tools#1030; no pin bump changes
it.
* It is STALE, and scoped to the comparator rather than the block.
The manifest pins the sha256 of the comparator GDS as committed
TODAY; this run's own `provenance.input.content_hash` is a
different, superseded vintage (2026-08-15, before the #215/#223
layout change), asserted below so the divergence is visible
rather than inferred. The TODAY side moved again at issue #356
(DR-0035, well taps and tie straps), which is why the
`artifacts` pin below is a third distinct hash; the run's own
vintage is untouched, so the gap this row records is now wider,
not narrower.
Consequently this citation must be RE-POINTED, not merely re-run,
before it can ever be read as met: a comparator-scoped pex run does
not carry a block-scoped item-7 claim. `expected_rows` pins the
current verdict in both directions, so a flip to `met` fails CI until
a human re-reads it.
The substantive post-layout evidence this repo does have -- five
extracted campaigns re-run against the current layout -- is real but
is not a `klt pex` report, and item 7 is the one item that rejects
every other evidence kind (klayout-tools#871). That gap is the
point of committing this row as it stands.
T1 item 8 (Characterization report), ANALOG partition. Issue #339.
THE ONLY CITATION IN THIS MANIFEST WHOSE ENVELOPE THIS REPO WROTE.
Item 8 names no `klt` verb, so no verb's output can satisfy it; the
grader ingests it through an opt-in generic evidence envelope
(`kind: generic`, klayout-tools#1152) a project hand-writes, and
item 8 is the only T1 item that accepts one. See
signoff/evidence/README.md for what that means and what it costs.
WHAT THE `met` MEANS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It means an aggregated,
per-spec-row characterization artifact exists and a human re-read it
against a named commit. It does NOT mean the design passes: THREE
RATIFIED ROWS FAIL in the document this cites -- ENOB (8.855 bits
worst, governing extracted, vs `> 9.0`), SFDR (60.41 dB vs
`>= 62 dB`) and Area (0.151827 mm^2 vs `< 0.1 mm^2`). Whether the
block passes its corner set is item 5, which is `unmet` on both
partitions. The checklist separates the two on purpose; so does this
entry, and so does the evidence record under signoff/records/.
WHY THE PINNED HASH IS THE DOCUMENT'S, NOT THE ENVELOPE'S. The
manifest's `content_hash` is compared against the cited envelope's
own `provenance.input.content_hash`, which here is the sha256 of
sim/characterization-summary.md -- so the pin is a freshness claim
about the RECORD, which is the thing that can rot, not about the
wrapper. `artifacts` below re-hashes that same file, which is what
makes the claim checkable on a pull request with no `klt` present.
REPO-SIDE CHECK IS STRONGER THAN THE GRADER'S HERE, for the second
time in this file (the first is 3.digital). `klt signoff` re-hashes
an envelope's named input only for the kinds whose input field it
knows; a `generic` envelope's author picks their own field names, so
the grader reports `input_verified: null` and the pin is compared
only against this envelope's own claim. `--check` hashes the
committed document directly.
T1 item 8 (Characterization report), DIGITAL partition. Issue #339.
SAME DOCUMENT, DIFFERENT SECTION, SEPARATE ENVELOPE. Item 8's own
text asks a digital partition for `Fmax, area, and power across the
corner set, not just functional pass/fail` -- which the analog
per-spec-row table does not carry. Those three quantities were
already measured and committed (`klt place-and-route` for area, the
five-corner post-route `klt sta` sweep for Fmax and estimated
power, both under design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/reports/); what did
not exist was an AGGREGATION of them. #339 wrote that section and
this envelope asserts it.
Two envelopes rather than one shared file, even though both wrap the
same document: this manifest keys every citation per partition (see
its own _comment), and a shared envelope would make the digital
row's verdict a restatement of the analog row's rather than a claim
about the digital partition's own evidence.
WHAT THE `met` DOES NOT MEAN: that this partition is verified. The
rung-2 gate-level SPICE replay is NOT passing -- six campaigns with
committed records, each one's latest reading FAIL or ERROR at the
re-read commit, under active root-causing -- and the routed macro
has neither an LVS compare nor an extracted SPEF. Those are items 4
and 5, both `unmet` on this partition. The wrapped section says all
three plainly rather than letting a green row imply otherwise.
THE FUNCTIONAL HALF IS A POINTER, DELIBERATELY. The gate-level
campaigns mint a record every day or two; transcribing their figures
would make the wrapped document stale the day it was written, which
is the exact defect issue #339 exists to close. The section names
the campaigns and their disposition and sends the reader to each
campaign's own latest record.
